defaultFolder.name: Default NPC folder
defaultFolder.hint: Root Actor folder used when the dashboard is set to the configured default destination. Leave empty to use the Actors root.

maxBatch.name: Maximum batch size
maxBatch.hint: Maximum number of NPC Actors that one generation or import action may create.

tierStyle.name: Tier style
tierStyle.hint: Choose whether NPC Button uses its named competence tiers or exact D&D 5e Challenge Ratings. CR mode exposes every standard CR from 0 through 30.

filters.name: Dashboard string filters
filters.hint: Open advanced allow/deny filters for picker-driven dashboard fields such as Roles, Races, Habitats, Group types, Naming styles, and Actor folders.
filters.label: Configure filters

filtersStorage.name: Dashboard string filters storage
filtersStorage.hint: Internal JSON storage for advanced dashboard string filters.

ui.intro: Configure NPCs once, then create them locally or use the same intent for an AI-generated Foundry payload.
ui.roleHint: Search or browse the hierarchical role catalog. The picker is virtualized so it stays responsive as the catalog grows.
ui.tierHint: Named competence tier. Change Tier style in Configure Settings to use exact CR values instead.
ui.challengeRatingHint: Choose any standard D&D 5e CR from 0, 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, and 1 through 30.
ui.raceHint: Search or browse preset races. To use any other race, type its name into the picker search and select the custom entry.
ui.useCustomRace: Use this text as a custom Race
ui.namingStyleHint: Search or browse naming palettes. The Help window shows clearly distinct examples for each style.
ui.wealthHint: Influences AI-generated money, equipment quality, personal possessions, and status items.
ui.seedPlaceholder: Optional reproducible seed for local generation
ui.seedHint: Local generation with the same options and seed reproduces the same generated data.
ui.destinationIntro: Choose where locally generated or AI-imported Actors are created.
ui.destinationHint: Browse the full Actor-folder hierarchy, choose the Actors root or configured default, or type a new root-folder name into search and select it.
ui.createRootFolder: Create or reuse a new root Actor folder with this name
ui.openLastActorHint: Opens up to 10 Actors. Up to three are visible side-by-side; later Actors are stacked behind them so closing a top sheet reveals the next one.
ui.aiIntro: Copy a detailed strict prompt into any AI conversation, copy its JSON reply, then import that reply into the destination above.
ui.manualPastePlaceholder: Paste the JSON reply here only if your browser blocks clipboard reading.
ui.groupTypeHint: Create independent NPCs or a coherent family, patrol, raider band, crew, caravan, council, and other group archetypes.
ui.habitatHint: Choose the environment and settlement context that shapes daily life, possessions, travel, and social assumptions. Type any other habitat to use it directly.
ui.useCustomHabitat: Use this text as a custom habitat
ui.groupConfigurationIntro: Advanced controls for relationships, internal structure, race mixing, and shared group context.
ui.suggestedGroupSizesHint: Shortcuts only; Count remains fully editable.
ui.raceCompositionHint: Use the main Race field for a single-race group or as the primary race when mixing several races.
ui.possibleRacesHint: Search and select any number of allowed races. Custom races can be added by typing them into the search.
ui.raceDistributionHint: Controls how strongly the primary Race dominates the generated group.
ui.raceWeightsHint: Relative weights; they do not need to add up to 100.
ui.groupBriefPlaceholder: Optional: local feud, family business, employer, current crisis, taboo, destination, shared objective…
ui.groupBriefHint: Passed into the AI prompt as additional context. Keep it focused on facts that should affect multiple NPCs.
ui.combatReadinessHint: Controls how heavily armed the NPC is relative to the Role. Weaponless always means no weapons or armor; higher levels remain constrained by what the occupation and situation can realistically justify.
ui.compositionIntro: Control how Race and Role are distributed across any multi-NPC batch, whether or not the NPCs form an intentional group.
ui.roleCompositionHint: The main Role selected above is always the primary Role. Mixed modes distribute only among Possible roles while preserving the exact batch Count.
ui.possibleRolesHint: Search and select the Roles allowed in a mixed-role batch. The main Role is automatically included and is always the primary Role.
ui.roleWeightsHint: Relative non-negative weights from 0 to 1000, not percentages. Higher numbers receive more NPCs; 0 excludes that Role when another Role has a positive weight. 10/20/30 is the same ratio as 1/2/3.
ui.weaponVarietyHint: Controls whether realistic role-appropriate weapons favor melee, ranged, or a mix. Hard-only modes never invent an implausible weapon just to satisfy the category.
ui.previewImportHint: Open a fast preview where NPCs can be selected/deselected and simple fields edited before final validation and Actor creation. Count mismatches open this preview automatically unless the global count-agnostic import setting is enabled.
ui.genderCompositionHint: Choose how male and female NPCs are distributed across the generated batch.
ui.primaryRoleNote: Primary Role: {role}. This is the Role selected in the main Role field above.
ui.preparedPromptHint: The generated prompt is kept here. If automatic clipboard access is blocked or Foundry is not focused, select the text or retry copying manually.
ui.raceExactCountsHint: Set the exact number of NPCs for every selected Race. The assigned total must equal Count.
ui.raceExactAssignedValid: Assigned {assigned} of {target}. Exact total is valid.
ui.raceExactAssignedInvalid: Assigned {assigned} of {target}. Remaining: {remaining}. Adjust counts or distribute evenly.

help.title: NPC Button Help
help.generationBody: The dashboard uses the same intent for deterministic local generation and the AI prompt workflow.
help.count: Type any allowed number directly, or use the common 1, 3, 5, and 10 shortcuts.
help.role: Defines the NPC's practical function and biases local ability scores and durability. It also strongly guides AI inventory and characterization.
help.tierStyleNamed: The world currently uses named tiers. Ordinary through Champion provide broad competence bands; Configure Settings can switch the world to exact CR selection.
help.tierStyleCr: The world currently uses CR tiers. Every standard D&D 5e CR from 0 through 30 is selectable and the AI prompt requests that exact CR.
help.race: The built-in Race picker contains all standard 2024 Player’s Handbook races. Typing a non-preset name offers it directly as a custom Race; mixed groups can select several preset or custom races.
help.wealth: Poor, Average, Well-Off, or Elite. The AI uses this to scale carried money, equipment quality, comfort items, and visible status.
help.seed: Local generation always has a reusable seed. If you leave Seed blank, the module creates one automatically, shows it back in the dashboard, and records it in every generated Actor biography and module metadata.
help.destination: The folder picker preserves the Actor hierarchy. It can target any nested folder, the Actors root, the configured default, or a newly named root folder.
help.pickersBody: Role, Race, Naming style, Habitat, Group type, Tier/CR, Actor folder, and mixed-race selection use searchable hierarchical lists. Large lists render only visible rows plus a small buffer so catalog growth and large folder trees remain responsive.
help.namingBody: Naming styles are broad fictional tonal palettes rather than historical or linguistic claims. Each style now includes a larger set of creative idiomatic examples; the same examples and style guidance are embedded into the copied AI prompt as tonal references rather than a finite name list.
help.actorReviewBody: When review opening is enabled, the module opens at most the first 10 created Actors. Up to three top sheets are arranged side-by-side. Additional sheets reuse those column positions behind the first row, so closing a top sheet exposes the next Actor in that stack.
help.aiBody: The module does not call an AI service itself. It creates a strict portable prompt carrying naming references, habitat, group structure, race mixture, wealth, relationship density, secrets, rumours, quirks, and inventory requirements; then it validates the returned Actor core and inventory requests before import.
help.aiStep1: Configure Count, Group type, Habitat, Role, Tier or CR, Race composition, Wealth, Naming style, and Destination.
help.aiStep2: Click Copy prompt and paste the prompt into an AI conversation.
help.aiStep3: Copy the AI's JSON-only reply to your clipboard.
help.aiStep4: Return to Foundry and click Import NPC. The current destination is applied locally.
help.aiValidation: The importer validates the JSON root shape and every Actor independently from the requested Count. A count mismatch triggers automatic preview by default rather than a fatal error; only the selected subset is revalidated immediately before creation. Canonical item lookups are resolved against D&D 5e equipment packs, while invented roleplay possessions remain safe loot Items.
help.groupType: Choose independent NPCs or an intentional group archetype. Group presets vary responsibilities and tell the AI to create shared history and useful internal roles instead of copies of one NPC.
help.habitat: Defaults to Forest Village. Habitat changes the expected daily life, possessions, travel assumptions, work, rumors, and social context.
help.standardRacesBody: The built-in Player’s Handbook 2024 catalog is: {races}. Custom races remain available through the same picker.
help.habitatsBody: Built-in environments cover ordinary settlements and more specialized regions, including {habitats}. Any other habitat can be typed as a custom entry.
help.groupsBody: Group presets include {groups}, plus further security, outlaw, travel, work, faith, and community structures. Count stays editable, while each preset exposes sensible size shortcuts.
help.groupsAdvanced: Advanced settings control family structure, cohesion, hierarchy, relationship density, internal conflict, allowed races, race distribution, custom weights, and an optional shared group brief.
help.portraitPromptBody: Generated or AI-imported NPC Actor sheets include a header button that copies a concise portrait prompt for exactly one full-body adult-anime image of that NPC.
help.filterBody: Configure Settings provides a dedicated filter menu. Each major dashboard catalog has a scalable searchable multi-select list with every current item included by default; deselect entries to hide them. Advanced allow/deny string and regex rules remain available, and filter profiles can be exported/imported as versioned JSON files or through the clipboard.
help.compositionBody: Composition works independently of group lore. Race can be single, strongly primary (for example roughly 8/1/1 in a ten-person three-Race batch), primary-majority, broadly mixed, or custom-weighted. Role composition uses the main Role field as the primary Role and then applies the selected distribution mode to the allowed Roles.
help.combatReadinessBody: Every NPC still has combat-capable statistics. The readiness setting controls carried weapons and armor. Weaponless forces none; higher settings are strictly role-relative, so a scholar or jurist never turns into a heavily armed warrior while guards, soldiers, and raiders scale naturally.
help.weaponVarietyBody: Melee only, Melee preference, Mixed, Ranged preference, and Ranged only bias or constrain carried weapons without overriding occupational realism. If a ranged-only jurist has no plausible ranged weapon, the correct result is no weapon rather than an absurd loadout.
help.importPreviewBody: Preview provides a selectable master list plus a compact editor. Every NPC starts selected; deselect any entry you do not want, edit simple fields, then import only the selected subset. If the parsed top-level JSON count differs from the dashboard Count, preview opens automatically with a warning so the discrepancy can be reviewed instead of failing early. GMs can enable Allow arbitrary NPC import counts to skip this automatic review for safe external/manual JSON arrays. Maximum batch size and Actor validation always remain enforced.
help.roleMixBody: The main Role selected in Generation is always the primary Role. For mixed modes, Possible roles defines the allowed pool; the primary Role is automatically included even if it was not manually selected. Integer quotas always add up to the requested Count.
help.roleMixWeights: Custom weights are relative ratios, not percentages. Larger numbers mean more NPCs. A weight of 0 excludes that Role as long as at least one other Role has a positive weight. 10/20/30, 1/2/3, and 100/200/300 are equivalent. If every weight is 0, the module safely falls back to equal weights.
help.roleMixRounding: When a proportion does not divide evenly into the batch size, the module uses proportional integer quotas and assigns leftover NPCs to the largest fractional remainders. This preserves the exact batch Count and stays as close as possible to the requested ratio.

roleMixModes.single: Every NPC uses the primary Role.
roleMixModes.variants: Every NPC keeps the primary Role, but practical subtypes of that Role are spread as evenly as possible before repeating.
roleMixModes.groupPreset: The first NPC uses the primary Role; remaining NPCs follow the selected group archetype’s built-in responsibility cycle. Independent batches remain the primary Role throughout.
roleMixModes.balanced: All allowed Roles receive equal weight.
roleMixModes.primary: The primary Role targets 70%; the remaining 30% is split evenly across the other allowed Roles.
roleMixModes.dominant: The primary Role targets 85%; the remaining 15% is split evenly across the other allowed Roles.
roleMixModes.weighted: Each allowed Role uses its entered relative weight.

roleMixExamples.variants: Primary Merchant → 10 Merchants with distinct merchant specializations before reuse.
roleMixExamples.groupPreset: Depends on Group type; for Independent NPCs with primary Merchant → 10 Merchant.
roleMixExamples.balanced: Merchant + Artisan + Guard → 4 Merchant, 3 Artisan, 3 Guard.
roleMixExamples.primary: Primary Merchant + Artisan + Guard → 7 Merchant, 2 Artisan, 1 Guard.
roleMixExamples.dominant: Primary Merchant + Artisan + Guard → 8 Merchant, 1 Artisan, 1 Guard.
roleMixExamples.weighted: Merchant 10, Artisan 20, Guard 30 → 2 Merchant, 3 Artisan, 5 Guard.

help.raceMixBody: The main Race selected in Generation is the primary Race. For mixed modes, Possible races defines the allowed pool; the primary Race is automatically included. Integer quotas always add up to the requested Count.
help.raceMixWeights: Custom Race weights are relative ratios, not percentages. Larger numbers mean more NPCs. A weight of 0 excludes that Race as long as at least one other Race has a positive weight. 10/20/30, 1/2/3, and 100/200/300 are equivalent. If every weight is 0, the module safely falls back to equal weights.
help.mixRounding: When a proportion does not divide evenly into the batch size, the module uses proportional integer quotas and assigns leftover NPCs to the largest fractional remainders. This preserves the exact batch Count and stays as close as possible to the requested ratio.

raceMixModes.single: Every NPC uses the primary Race.
raceMixModes.dominant: The primary Race targets 85%; the remaining 15% is split evenly across the other allowed Races.
raceMixModes.primary: The primary Race targets 70%; the remaining 30% is split evenly across the other allowed Races.
raceMixModes.balanced: All allowed Races receive equal weight.
raceMixModes.weighted: Each allowed Race uses its entered relative weight.
raceMixModes.mixed: Legacy compatibility mode; the saved Race distribution setting determines the effective mix.
raceMixModes.exact: Uses the exact integer count entered for every selected Race. Counts must sum to Count.

raceMixExamples.dominant: Primary Human + Elf + Dwarf → 8 Human, 1 Elf, 1 Dwarf.
raceMixExamples.primary: Primary Human + Elf + Dwarf → 7 Human, 2 Elf, 1 Dwarf.
raceMixExamples.balanced: Human + Elf + Dwarf → 4 Human, 3 Elf, 3 Dwarf.
raceMixExamples.weighted: Human 10, Elf 20, Dwarf 30 → 2 Human, 3 Elf, 5 Dwarf.
raceMixExamples.mixed: Not shown in the current dashboard; retained only for older saved configurations.
raceMixExamples.exact: Count 10: Human 8, Elf 1, Dwarf 1 means exactly 8 / 1 / 1.

combatReadinessModes.weaponless: No weapons or armor. Occupational tools remain ordinary tools.
combatReadinessModes.minimal: Noncombatants stay effectively unarmed; inherently martial Roles receive at least one simple, plausible weapon.
combatReadinessModes.standard: Normal equipment for the Role during ordinary duties.
combatReadinessModes.prepared: Adds believable backup or protective gear when the Role supports it.
combatReadinessModes.armed: Maximum realistic preparedness for that exact Role; occupational ceilings still apply.

combatReadinessExamples.weaponless: Soldier → no weapon and no armor; Baker → work tools only.
combatReadinessExamples.minimal: Guard → one simple duty weapon; Scholar → normally no dedicated weapon.
combatReadinessExamples.standard: Guard → practical weapon and ordinary duty protection.
combatReadinessExamples.prepared: Scout → primary weapon plus plausible backup and light protection.
combatReadinessExamples.armed: Soldier → several sensible combat options; Jurist → at most discreet self-defense gear.

weaponVarietyModes.meleePreferred: Strongly favor melee; a ranged backup is allowed only when plausible.
weaponVarietyModes.mixed: Use a natural mix when the Role realistically supports both categories.
weaponVarietyModes.rangedPreferred: Strongly favor ranged; a melee backup is allowed only when plausible.
weaponVarietyModes.rangedOnly: Allow dedicated ranged weapons only; never invent one for a Role that has no realistic option.

weaponVarietyExamples.meleePreferred: Guard → Spear or Longsword favored; crossbow only as a sensible backup.
weaponVarietyExamples.mixed: Soldier → melee and ranged options may both appear.
weaponVarietyExamples.rangedPreferred: Scout → Shortbow favored with a knife or Shortsword only as backup.
weaponVarietyExamples.rangedOnly: Jurist with no plausible ranged option → weaponless rather than implausibly armed.

normal.behavior: Uses the configured preview toggle. If preview is off, validated Actors can proceed directly to creation.

mismatch.behavior: Preview opens automatically with a warning. Every NPC is initially selected, so extras can be deselected before import.

arbitrary.behavior: Safe external/manual arrays may proceed without forced mismatch preview; normal validation still applies.

oversized.behavior: Safety limits remain enforced; the count setting never bypasses the configured maximum batch size.

items.behavior: All current catalog items start included. Deselect an item to hide it from the matching dashboard picker; extension-added items remain included by default unless explicitly excluded.

advanced.behavior: Optional exact, contains, prefix, suffix, and regular-expression allow/deny rules refine the item selection. Deny rules take precedence.

profiles.behavior: Export or import the complete filter configuration as versioned JSON so a ready-configured setup can be reused or transferred.

notifications.gmOnly: Only a Game Master can create NPCs with Runyth NPC Button.
notifications.promptCopied: AI NPC prompt copied to the clipboard.
notifications.portraitPromptCopied: Portrait prompt copied to the clipboard.
notifications.filtersCopied: Filter profile JSON copied to the clipboard.
notifications.filterProfileTooLarge: Filter profile is too large to import.
notifications.promptCopyManual: AI prompt prepared, but automatic clipboard access is unavailable. The prompt is preserved below for manual copying.
notifications.clipboardUnavailable: Automatic clipboard access is unavailable. The prepared content remains available for manual copying.

errors.clipboardWrite: Clipboard writing is not available in this client.
errors.clipboardRead: Clipboard reading is not available or was blocked by the browser.
errors.manualPasteFallback: Open the manual-paste section, paste the AI JSON there, and click Import NPC again.
errors.portraitPromptUnavailable: This Actor does not contain Runyth NPC Button generation metadata.
errors.raceExactCountMismatch: Exact Race counts assign {assigned} NPCs, but Count is {target}. Adjust the exact counts first.

namingDescriptions.central: Balanced town-and-road names with restrained surnames; broadly settled and neutral in tone.
namingDescriptions.coastal: Open-vowel given names and maritime surnames suggesting ports, fishing communities, and sea trade.
namingDescriptions.highland: Harder consonants and landscape-heavy surnames suggesting uplands, stone settlements, and old local lineages.
namingDescriptions.frontier: Short practical names and occupational or settlement surnames suggesting farms, trades, border villages, and new communities.

filters.title: NPC Button string filters
filters.intro: Use the selected-item lists for ordinary filtering. Every current item is selected by default; deselect an item to hide it from the corresponding dashboard picker. Advanced allow/deny string and regex rules remain available below each list.

placeholders.roles: Filter visible role entries by id, label, description, or search text.
placeholders.races: Filter visible race entries, including extension races and custom picker suggestions.
placeholders.namingStyles: Curate which naming palettes may be selected in the dashboard.
placeholders.habitats: Restrict or focus the environment presets shown in the habitat picker.
placeholders.groupTypes: Allow or hide specific group archetypes such as families or guard patrols.
placeholders.folders: Curate which Actor-folder targets appear in the destination picker.

itemPicker.label: Included items
itemPicker.hint: All available items are selected by default. Deselect individual entries to exclude them from the dashboard. The list is searchable, hierarchical, scrollable, and virtualized for large catalogs.

preview.title: NPC import preview
preview.editorHint: Edit only the simple table-facing fields you need. The complete payload is validated again before import.
preview.name: Name
preview.biographyHint: Keep the required labeled biography sections. Unsupported HTML is sanitized during final import.
preview.countMismatchNotice: The dashboard requested {expected} NPCs, but the parsed top-level JSON contains {actual}. Review the batch and deselect any NPCs you do not want to import.
preview.maximumNotice: The payload exceeds the configured maximum batch size of {max}. Deselect entries until the selected batch is within the limit.
preview.includeNpc: Include this NPC in the import
preview.selectAtLeastOne: Select at least one NPC to import.

manualCopy.title: Manual copy
manualCopy.hint: Automatic clipboard access was unavailable. The prepared content is preserved below; select it for Ctrl+C or retry the browser clipboard action.
manualCopy.selected: Text selected. Press Ctrl+C to copy it.
manualCopy.unavailable: Clipboard access is still unavailable. The text is selected for manual copying.
